body:
DREW RULINGS (2026-10-29, main chat):

1. **Dependabot — keep it simple.** If an alert's fix is a quick merge-and-fix (minutes, won't take everything down): just do it. Everything else is LOWEST priority — group the rest into a couple of dependency-update PRs and stop there; we only dig into the pile if every other issue is figured out. A giant critical that can't be updated does NOT stop the fleet — it gets worked only when there is spare bandwidth under the burn policy (#2173's under-paced pools are exactly that bandwidth). The scout-triage design in this issue is rescoped to match: quick-win pass + grouping, not a deep remediation program.
2. **JULES_API_KEY: install it fleet-wide** (all four repos). Dispatched 2026-10-29.
3. **Scout triage for ALL issues: approved** — the classifier idea generalizes from CI failures to incoming issues generally.
4. **Use the Jules API more: approved** — first-class queue executor work proceeds.
5. **ChatGPT scheduled tasks: opportunistic** — use them where a good fit is found (with the self-reporting convention); if a placement turns out to be a problem, it goes on the not-dealing-with list. Otherwise route through the other scheduled-task systems.
6. **Claude scheduled tasks:** verdict accepted as answered — even if paid, not really useful for us, for the same fire-and-forget reason as ChatGPT Tasks (no result read-back). No seat purchase.

JULES_API_KEY gap fixed 2026-10-29T07:47Z: the Jules API key was in Bitwarden Secrets Manager (google.jules-api-key) and is now installed fleet-wide as the JULES_API_KEY Actions secret in developing-today/code (07:47:02Z), developing-today/opencode (07:47:06Z), developing-today/openchamber (07:47:09Z), and dezren39/nix (07:47:13Z) — verified per repo via gh secret list. Opencode's Jules-first leg of the main-broken chain can now fire.

## Intake review

- **Fleet monitor intake** (repo-fleet-monitor, 2026-10-29 run): filed with no labels at all. Normalized: `kind/enhancement`, `source/human` (Drew directive, 2026-10-29), `status/needs-triage`, `priority/normal`, `effort/l`, `meta/enriched`. The body already carries an `## Acceptance` section, so no acceptance section was appended.
- **Related:** main-broken chain design #1779 §5 (the classifier leg lands there), #2177/#2171 (executor-surface comparisons), the opencode JULES_API_KEY gap named in the acceptance is also why opencode main-broken filings (e.g. #850) note Jules was not engaged.
- **Risks:** four separable workstreams in one issue (Dependabot triage, the JULES_API_KEY gap, the classifier leg, the ChatGPT allowance check) — expect this to split into per-jewel follow-ups at triage rather than land as one change.
- **Suggested approach:** start with the two one-step items (JULES_API_KEY gap verdict, ChatGPT allowance verification), then the Dependabot grouped report, then the classifier leg dry-run in one repo.
